newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin choses moderate Rybkin to succeed Lebed.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin choses moderate Rybkin to succeed Lebed.

text.p: Russian President Boris Yeltsin named moderate politician Ivan Rybkin on Saturday to succeed ousted Alexander Lebed in two posts -- secretary of the powerful Security Council and his envoy to rebel Chechnya.
The announcement was made by the Kremlin press service.
Yeltsin dramatically sacked Lebed on Thursday as his security supremo, accusing him in a televised speech of lack of team spirit and naked presidential ambitions.
On Saturday, he dismissed him as his personal representative in breakaway Chechnya.
Chechen separatists, with whom Lebed brokered a peace deal on August 31, have warned that Lebed's dismissal could lead to a deterioration of the situation there.
Rybkin, who turns 50 on Sunday, was speaker of the State Duma lower house of parliament from 1993 to 1995.
A communist, he was elected as a member of the conservative Agrarian Party, but broke with it after becoming the head of the parliament and becoming a Yeltsin ally.

He is a moderate who firmly steered the Duma away from any clashes with the president. After the 1995 parliamentary election, Rybkin failed to win a second term as speaker because the communists and their allies voted against him.
